caption: Moore v. Illinois
node: the-right-to-counsel/Lineups and the Right to Counsel (also fair-trial/Eyewitness Identification)
justification: Direct hop-1 omission from the Wade/Gilbert/Kirby/Ash seed cluster. Holds that a corporeal identification of the accused at a POST-CHARGE PRELIMINARY HEARING, conducted with no counsel present (and after the witness was told a suspect would be produced, heard his name called, and heard the prosecutor recite the implicating evidence), is a Sixth Amendment critical stage under Wade/Gilbert — the prosecution may not buttress its case-in-chief with the uncounseled pretrial identification even on a proof of independent source (the Gilbert per se rule for the pretrial ID itself), and it extends Wade beyond the stationhouse lineup to a one-on-one courtroom showup. Genuinely fills the placed-empty Lineups stub and is the strongest single-showup application of the counsel-at-identification right the corpus lacks. grep 0 (only Virginia v. Moore present). Identification-facing = squarely in remit (REMIT GUARD keeps 'identifications').
